7.4.3.3.3 ComIPdu based proxy handling
If using a data path in Com that refers to ComIPdus, then a ComUserModuleCnf is required for each EcucPartition, in which the Com Proxy
• requires direct access to the Com APIs initiating transmission requests
• provides notification callbacks w.r.t transmission and reception Effectively, a SwCluCComProxyBaseSocket links a fixed set of notification callbacks in the Com to a specific EcucPartition in the Com Proxy. As a consequence, the Com Proxy has to map each ComUserIPdu via ComUserSystemTemplateSystemSignalRef to an ComIPdu. Even if the concept of Com user provides a lot of flexibility to support access by multiple users, including their notifications, some limitations need to be considered. In general, multiple writers can cause race conditions, if the writers are not coordinated. In addition, the behavior of <ComUser_ComCbkTriggerTransmit> does not support multiple notified users for the same ComIPdu. Since such a coordination across different Software Clusters is hardly achievable, the following restriction applies: module
[SWS_SwCluC_CONSTR_03546] Multiplicity of provided ComIPdus Status: DRAFT Upstream requirements: SRS_SwCluC_00211
⌈Sent ComIPdu shall be provided to at most one Application Software Cluster.⌋ In addition, the Com Proxy does not support a fan out of ComIPdus sent or received via transport protocol API. Please note that the PduR supports a fan-out of TP-connections to upper layers.
